assumptions: The initial product remains a bounded reconciliation and exception-routing sidecar: it does not create a legally dispositive eCMR, certify authenticity, decide liability, give a collectability guarantee, or act as the eFTI platform used for regulatory submissions.

The first implementation is limited to one permissioned factor or regional TMS, one country-pair workflow, and a small configured document set; legal review, security work, and exceptional document handling can be contracted within the stated capital and founder-time constraints.
The proposed pricing, margin progression, partner-channel payback, shipment volume, and founder-value path are planning hypotheses rather than established results.

No reusable data advantage is assumed unless a partner expressly grants rights to use de-identified rejection and cure outcomes; absent that permission, the initial advantage is workflow-specific reconciliation knowledge only.
A competent team makes extensive use of AI for extraction, matching, mapping, and operations, while qualified humans remain responsible for legal boundaries, security, and ambiguous exceptions.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A paid anchor-partner pilot should measure the baseline share and value of invoices blocked by document defects, integration cost and elapsed time, straight-through clearance, false-positive and false-negative costs, manual minutes per exception, reduction in funding or payment delay, realized gross margin, and the partner's willingness to renew, expand volume, and permit reusable de-identified cure labels.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The idea targets a concrete control point: completed transport does not become fundable or payment-ready until invoice, order, CMR/POD, signatures, reservations, and accessorial evidence reconcile. Cross-system normalization is a more specific insight than another document store, although the evidence does not yet show that this gap is frequent enough outside the cited workflows.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Buyer terms and factoring requirements directly establish that incomplete proof can delay the payment clock or funding, making the underlying cash-flow pain credible and recurrent. However, broad late-payment evidence does not isolate document defects, and there is no direct evidence that a factor, forwarder, or TMS will pay separately for this sidecar rather than change its rules or use an incumbent feature; that is important uncertainty, not evidence of no demand.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: A platform minimum plus per-check and managed-exception fees can align revenue with repeated funding or payment decisions and could develop attractive software margins once mappings stabilize. The proposed 50-70% pilot margin, 72-86% mature margin, sub-12-month payback, and 940,000-check scale case are unvalidated; bespoke integrations, manual exceptions, enterprise sales, and channel share could materially compress contribution margin and owner earnings.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Poland's unusually large road-freight activity supplies a substantial recurring base, while one factor or regional TMS, one country pair, and one document set form a suitably narrow initial segment. Tonne-kilometres do not reveal the number of addressable checks, the relevant customer mix, or the portion of invoices blocked by correctable evidence defects, so the beachhead's revenue depth remains uncertain.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: A neutral reconciler spanning otherwise fragmented systems could own a narrow factor-specific decision layer. Yet Dashdoc already links eCMR evidence to invoicing and Transporeon already performs payment-ready verification and dispute handling with native data; both control workflow and distribution, so the sidecar currently lacks a demonstrated route to a particularly strong position.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A successful embedded funding check could extend to additional partner portfolios, country pairs, evidence types, forwarder accounts-payable workflows, and priced exception services. Each adjacency benefits from a common reconciliation layer, but contractual variation, local legal rules, and heterogeneous schemas may make expansion closer to repeated integration work than low-cost replication.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Embedding the checks in funding release can create workflow switching costs, and permissioned labeled rejection-and-cure outcomes could improve exception ranking over time. Those rights are not established, the anchor partner controls the source data, and incumbent TMS/eCMR/freight-audit platforms can bundle similar logic, leaving the proposed moat contingent rather than inherent.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Cross-system reconciliation, visible source trails, and early exception routing could be materially more useful than siloed uploads where a partner has fragmented inputs. No evidence yet establishes superior coverage, lower review cost, faster funding, or acceptable false-positive rates versus native factor rules, Dashdoc, or Transporeon, so the behavior-changing magnitude of the advantage is unresolved.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Legal recognition of compliant eCMR, the 2027 eFTI acceptance milestone, a large Polish freight base, and persistent payment delays support continued freight digitization and document interoperability. Paper remains permissible, the sidecar must maintain a careful certification boundary, and the same digitization trend strengthens platforms already capable of absorbing the feature.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: One factor or TMS integration could efficiently activate recurring portfolio volume and avoids uneconomic carrier-by-carrier acquisition. No partner commitment, data access, marketplace route, sales-cycle evidence, or channel economics exists, and the proposed distributor can also become the builder or buyer of an incumbent module; enterprise relationship selling is also a demanding fit for this part-time founder.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: Document extraction, entity matching, and exception ranking fit the founder's data-science and AI leverage, and a tightly scoped pilot can plausibly fit the stated 85,000 PLN and 18-25 weekly hours. Execution still requires authorized access, partner integration, privacy and security controls, precise legal positioning, reliable audit trails, low false-positive rates, and bounded manual review; cross-border customization or sustained partner support could exceed the founder's time ceiling.

highest_value_structural_change: Make a factor the contracted system-of-decision customer across multiple heterogeneous TMS/eCMR sources, with minimum recurring volume and rights to normalized de-identified rejection and cure outcomes, so the product owns the funding-release rules and learning loop rather than remaining an optional carrier-facing readiness score.
main_structural_strength: The product can sit at a repeated, economically consequential control point immediately before funding or payment release, where faster reconciliation has measurable cash-flow value and one embedded integration can generate portfolio-scale usage.
primary_score_limiter: The opportunity depends on a factor or TMS simultaneously granting source-data access, adopting an external decision layer, delivering recurring volume, and paying separately even though that partner or an incumbent platform can internalize the feature.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Transporeon already offers payment-ready freight verification and dispute workflow using native platform data, while Dashdoc already carries eCMR evidence through invoicing; this directly weakens the claim that a standalone sidecar has a durable or sufficiently superior wedge.
